content: The following is a detailed explanation of the skills required for an Emergency Medical Technician-Basic (EMT-B) as outlined by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT): 1. Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR): EMT-Bs must be proficient in performing CPR to restore circulation and breathing in patients experiencing cardiac arrest. 2. Airway, Oxygen, and Ventilation Skills: Upper Airway Adjuncts and Suction: EMT-Bs must be able to use devices such as oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal airways to maintain an open airway. They must also be skilled in suctioning to clear obstructions. Oropharyngeal Airway (OPA): This device is used to keep the airway open in unconscious patients without a gag reflex. Nasopharyngeal Airway (NPA): This device is used to maintain an open airway in patients who may have a gag reflex or cannot tolerate an OPA. Suctioning: EMT-Bs must be able to remove secretions, blood, or vomit from the airway to prevent aspiration and maintain patency. 3. Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM) Ventilation: EMT-Bs must be skilled in using a bag-valve-mask to provide ventilation to apneic patients or those with inadequate respiratory effort. 4. Bleeding Control and Shock Management: Body Substance Isolation (BSI): EMT-Bs must use appropriate personal protective equipment to prevent exposure to bodily fluids. Emergency Bleeding Control: Techniques such as direct pressure, tourniquets, and hemostatic agents must be employed to control severe bleeding. Dressing Wounds: EMT-Bs must apply appropriate dressings and bandages to manage wounds and prevent further contamination. 5. Cardiac Arrest Management and Automated External Defibrillator (AED): EMT-Bs must perform CPR and use an AED to deliver defibrillation to patients in cardiac arrest. 6. Immobilization Skills: EMT-Bs must immobilize joint injuries, long bone fractures, and use traction splinting when necessary. Proper splinting techniques are essential to prevent further injury. 7. Mouth-to-Mask Ventilation with Supplemental Oxygen: EMT-Bs must be able to provide effective ventilation using a mask and supplemental oxygen. 8. Oxygen Administration: EMT-Bs must administer oxygen using various devices, including: Bag-valve-mask (BVM) Nasal cannula Non-rebreather mask Simple face mask 9. Patient Assessment and Management (Medical): EMT-Bs must conduct a thorough assessment of the patient, including: Identifying signs and symptoms. Asking about allergies, medications, past medical history, last oral intake, and events leading to the current condition. Measuring vital signs and determining the need for interventions or transport. Performing a detailed physical examination, including assessing for deformities, contusions, abrasions, penetrations, burns, tenderness, lacerations, and swelling. Evaluating the onset, provocation, quality, radiation, severity, and timing of symptoms (OPQRST). Documenting the description of the episode, including onset, duration, associated symptoms, evidence of trauma, and any interventions performed. 10. Special Considerations in Patient Assessment: Allergic Reactions: EMT-Bs must determine the allergen, the method of exposure, the effects, progression of symptoms, and any interventions performed. Substance Ingestion or Exposure: EMT-Bs must assess the type of substance, time of exposure, quantity ingested, duration of exposure, and any interventions performed. They must also estimate the patient’s weight and consider environmental factors. Pregnancy-Related Emergencies: EMT-Bs must assess the duration of pregnancy, presence of pain or contractions, bleeding or discharge, the urge to push, and the date of the last menstrual period. Behavioral Emergencies: EMT-Bs must evaluate the patient’s mental state, determine suicidal tendencies, and assess whether the patient poses a threat to themselves or others. They must also rule out underlying medical problems and provide appropriate interventions. 11. Interventions and Transport: EMT-Bs must determine the need for immediate interventions and decide on the appropriate mode of transport to a medical facility. These skills are essential for EMT-Bs to provide effective prehospital care and ensure the safety and well-being of their patients.
